Screen usage context: college offense ran high screen volume with Tyson. screen_yard_share estimate ~40-50% of targets (proxy; precise yard-share not confirmed). screen_yard_share NOT encoded — film review overrides proxy concern (see below).
Film review (2026-04-11, user-conducted):
vs Texas State: lined up slot vs press man, beats press at 5 yards off LOS, wins outside leverage, adjusts frame on 40-yard gain with 1-handed contested catch while safety crashes — press win + vertical tracking + contested finish.
vs Baylor: boundary short side, corner route up the seam in Cover 2, splits DB and LB, reads space and attacks window — spatial feel and route utility, not gadget spam.
vs TCU (post): strong side boundary vs soft man, wins inside leverage on post for 15-yard gain — leverage win creating viable throwing window.
vs TCU (60-yd TD): weak side boundary vs press man, sells screen look initially then torches press over the top for 60-yard walk-in TD — weaponizes screen expectation, which is the key distinction: manufactured usage may have been deployment choice, not ceiling.
Model philosophy note: screen-yard share = production-translation risk, not evidence that the receiver cannot play. Film confirms press wins, leverage wins, vertical tracking, contested catch ability, and boundary route success. Screen-heavy college deployment reflects offense exploiting an easy button on a better-than-deployed player. screen_yard_share penalty WILL NOT be applied unless hard data confirms and film evidence is re-evaluated. deep_yard_share remains a valid caution flag if confirmed.

Michigan transfer to SMU who posted 31 catches for 436 yards and 4 TDs in 2025; standout combine with a 4.57 40 and 37-inch vertical demonstrating above-average athleticism. Senior Bowl performer rising on draft boards with upside as a receiving TE2.

First-team All-ACC in 2025 with 47 catches for 468 yards and 7 TDs, leading NC State with his red-zone presence; did not run the 40 at the combine due to a hamstring injury. Natural pass catcher with strong hands and zone feel but undersized frame raises NFL ceiling questions.

Blocking-first TE at Ohio State with just 15 catches for 168 yards and 2 TDs in 2025; used primarily to open holes in Ohio State's run-heavy sets. Limited receiving upside but respected as a technician in pass protection and short-area blocking.

Converted linebacker — played LB at Kansas State before transferring to Oklahoma, where he switched to TE in 2025 and produced 44 catches for 533 yards with All-SEC Third Team recognition; elite 4.52 40-dash for the position reflects LB athleticism. Extreme developmental upside with only one year of TE experience.

Blocking-and-receiving TE at Tennessee with 26 catches for 261 yards and 2 TDs in 2025; heavy NFL-ready frame at 6'5", 259 lbs but 4.90 40 time is a red flag for receiving role upside. Projects as a late-round blocking TE2/developmental prospect.

German-born, rare athletic specimen at 6'6" with a 4.61 40 and exceptional combine testing; only 24 catches for 248 yards in 2025 as Michigan's blocking TE in a run-heavy scheme. Elite developmental upside if he refines route running and receives more targets.

Led all FBS tight ends in receptions (74) and contested-catch percentage (74.1%) in 2025 with 727 yards and 6 TDs at Houston; at 6'7" he is a red-zone mismatch with massive catch radius. Below-average athleticism after the catch limits YAC but his size and hands project well as a move TE2.

Son of Super Bowl champion Russell Maryland, posted 27 catches for 322 yards and 2 TDs at SMU in 2025 with elite seam speed (4.51 40) and alignment versatility; finished career as SMU's all-time leader in TE receiving yards. Receiving instincts and athleticism are clear, but blocking and route refinement need work.

Five-year USC starter who posted 30 catches for 450 yards and 4 TDs in his final season; two prior ACL tears (high school and 2023 at USC) raise durability flags. Smooth route runner with good hands but testing data from the combine was not publicly available.

Starter on Indiana's undefeated 2025 regular season squad with 32 catches for 387 yards and 2 TDs plus a rushing score; reliable blocker and intermediate target for the Big Ten champion Hoosiers. Best suited as an H-back/move TE in creative schemes.

6'7" frame with 32 catches for 482 yards in 2025 at Notre Dame; missed nearly two full seasons recovering from double ACL tears early in his career. Legitimate injury history clouds his floor but his size-speed combination and length at the catch point project as a moldable Y-TE.

Late-blooming five-year TCU TE who finally broke out with 34 catches for 319 yards and 2 TDs in 2025 as the starter; did not run the 40 or perform drills at the combine. PFF ranks him 292nd overall; projects as a Day 3 depth/blocking TE.

49 catches for 545 yards and 2 TDs in 2025, leading ACC TEs in receiving yards; posted the best 3-cone (7.08) among all TEs at the combine and a 38.5-inch vertical that locked up Day 2 consideration. Old-school Y-TE with elite effort and blocking willingness; drop issues need to be cleaned up.

Ohio State transfer who posted 29 catches for 416 yards and 4 TDs in 2025 final year at Cincinnati; returned for senior season specifically to be the first TE taken in 2026. Excellent hands and zone feel, but did not perform combine drills; blocking development is his NFL key.

Unique background: started as a QB at Southeastern Louisiana, transferred to Oklahoma (2024, 42 catches) then LSU (2025, 24 catches for 252 yards and 2 TDs). Journey player with multi-position athleticism but limited TE production at power programs.

Two-time All-America TE at Baylor with 50 catches for 694 yards and 6 TDs in 2025, finishing 2nd nationally in TE receiving yards; hamstring pull forced him to shut down all combine testing. Three-time consensus All-American; contested-catch ability and vertical athleticism are elite but blocking needs major development.

39 catches for 635 yards and 5 TDs at Ole Miss in 2025 with a 16.3 YPC average that ranked among the nation's best for TEs; played through an undisclosed injury all season. Aligned all over the formation with big-play ability, though he skipped combine drills and blocking is a notable weakness.
